distractors.reason: We don't say 'big time' to mean spare time. 'Big' describes size, not the time you have to relax.
We don't say 'fast time'. 'Fast' describes speed, so it doesn't fit with time you have for hobbies.
We don't say 'high time' for free time. 'High' describes height or level, not time you have to relax.

l1_interference: Los hispanohablantes a veces colocan el adjetivo despues del sustantivo, como 'time free', en lugar de 'free time'. En ingles el adjetivo va antes del sustantivo.
explanation: In English, the adjective normally comes before the noun. 'Free' describes time that is not taken by work or school, so we say 'free time'.

related_collocations.example: I like to listen to loud music after school.
This is a good book about football.
We sometimes eat fast food on Fridays.

memory_tip: FREE TIME = the time you are not working or studying. In English, the adjective goes BEFORE the noun.
